newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-ENGLAND FAVOURITES FOR 1ST TEST VS NZ.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND FAVOURITES FOR 1ST TEST VS NZ.

text.p: England's cricketers go into their first test match against New Zealand at Eden Park on Friday odds-on favourites despite a fitness cloud hanging over key paceman Dominic Cork.
In stark contrast to the Zimbabwe leg of their tour, England's preparation for the New Zealand test series has been just about perfect.
They notched up impressive wins in their two warm-up matches, trouncing a New Zealand Selection by an innings and 113 runs, and Northern Districts by 10 wickets.
"Both victories have been comprehensive," said England skipper Mike Atherton. "Everybody's had a run and everyone's pretty confident."

New Zealand's test warm-up, on the other hand, could not have been worse. Their test batsmen were embarrassed by a trio of provincial bowlers in a two-day practice match on an Eden Park pitch this week, while their bowlers were unable to match their opponents' feats with the ball.
And several of New Zealand's key test players had their confidence badly bruised when they failed miserably playing for the Selection against the tourists.
England's only concerns are Atherton's batting, which has not improved since Zimbabwe, and Cork's back injury.
Cork was instrumental in setting up the win against Northern Districts, tearing through New Zealand opening test batsmen Bryan Young and Blair Pocock with consummate ease.

England coach David Lloyd has given Cork until Thursday to prove his fitness, but he won't be taking any chances with his potent new-ball strike bowler. Cork may miss the first test to ensure he is fit for the second and third.

In left-arm swing bowler Alan Mullally, England have a fine replacement for Cork. He took four for 52 in Northern Districts' second innings and, irrespective of Cork's injury woes, seems sure to make the first test side.

But England must decide whether to play both spinners -- left-armer Phil Tufnell and offspinner Robert Croft -- along with two fast-medium bowlers and allrounder Craig White, or leave out one spinner to bolster their seam attact.
Eden Park groundsman Ray Moffat said the pace bowlers should be able to extract good bounce out of the pitch, but it will also start to take turn as the test progresses.
